captive_summary: No public source found documents this specific vessel's onboard power-generation equipment. The FSRU is a 1977-built Moss-type LNG carrier (ex-Khannur) converted by Keppel/Jurong Shipyard in 2011-2012; Moss-type steam-turbine carriers of this era generically retain steam turbo-generators fed by dual-fuel (boil-off-gas/fuel-oil) boilers after FSRU conversion, but no source found ties that generic industry practice to THIS vessel specifically, so it cannot be asserted as a documented positive. Its regasification output instead feeds PLN's Jakarta-West Java grid (direction-test finding, see notes) -- the reverse of a captive-power relationship.
confirmed_how: Wartsila reference page and Riviera Maritime Media ('Oldest FSRU delivers decade-long uninterrupted regasification service') describe the Khannur-to-FSRU conversion (500 MMcf/d send-out, 0.25% boil-off rate) but neither discloses onboard generator/engine specifications. Multiple searches (DuckDuckGo, shipping-data.com, Wikipedia-style registries) turned up no vessel-specific engine/generator documentation.

hardware_summary: Mixed-refrigerant and propane-cycle gas turbines drive the refrigeration compressors across the LNG trains (mechanical drive; described as 'heavy-duty gas turbines' in Baker Hughes' long-term service scope); exhaust heat from these gas turbines is recovered via Heat Recovery Steam Generators (HRSG) driving steam turbines that generate electricity, used on-site and with surplus historically sold to PLN (4 MW cited for a village-electrification program). Exact turbine model/count and total generating MW not disclosed in sources found.
fuel_basis: Gas-fired: the ADB ESIA explicitly attributes the HRSG's energy input to 'the off-gas from the gas turbines,' and those same gas turbines are separately identified in the ESIA as 'Mixed Refrigerant and Propane Gas Turbines' (i.e. fed by plant process/feed gas, not diesel).
captive_summary: Confirmed on-site power generation via waste-heat recovery: the Tangguh Expansion Project (Train 3) ESIA states IFC Performance Standard 3 (resource/energy efficiency) 'is met with the installed heat recovery system using the off-gas from the gas turbines as energy input. Produced electricity is used internally and sold to Indonesia's state electricity company PLN.' This is a partially-captive, mixed mechanical-drive + power-generation site: mechanical-drive gas turbines run the refrigeration compressors, and their waste heat generates electricity used on-site (captive) with the surplus exported to PLN.
mechanical_drive_note: 'Mixed Refrigerant and Propane Gas Turbines' drive the refrigeration compressors across Trains 1-3 (ADB ESIA, listed among the TEP's main gaseous-emission sources); Baker Hughes' 90-month service agreement (2025) separately confirms 'heavy-duty gas turbines, steam turbines, and compressors for three LNG trains.' Aggregate shaft MW not disclosed in any source found.
confirmed_how: ADB project document 49222-001-esia-03.pdf ('Tangguh Expansion Project Environmental and Social Impact Assessment Executive Summary,' prepared by PT Greencap Indonesia), para 5.31: 'IFC PS 3 requires resource conservation and energy efficiency measures to be incorporated into projects. In the case of the TEP this requirement is met with the installed heat recovery system using the off-gas from the gas turbines as energy input. Produced electricity is used internally and sold to Indonesia's state electricity company PLN to serve the local electricity grid providing electricity to the nearby host villages.' Same document, para 1.2: TEP supports 'local electricity demand by allocating gas produced under the TEP as fuel for electric generators... Support the improvement of local livelihoods... by selling excess power produced by TEP to the State Electricity Company (PLN).' Section 5.58 separately notes 'Tangguh provides 4MW of power to the national electricity company PLN for electrification of local villages' under the original T1/T2 program. Corroborated independently by Turbomachinery International/Baker Hughes reporting on the plant's heavy-duty gas turbine and steam turbine fleet.
